worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}y\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y+z+2}y\,dx]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y+z+2}y\,dx]dA & ={∬}_{D}y[x]_{x=0}^{x=y+z+2}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}y(y+z+2)\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}+yz+2y\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate the double integral above over the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/b473cc75dbbd6fa36ba43f6bbdec4a0133164e6fd8bc5f76ff86cec74714a256.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{y}^{2}+yz+2y\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-y}{y}^{2}+yz+2y\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2-y}{y}^{2}+yz+2y\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[({y}^{2}+2y)z+\frac{1}{2}y{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=2-y}dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({y}^{2}+2y)(2-y)+\frac{1}{2}y(2-y)^{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(4y-{y}^{3})+\frac{1}{2}y(4-4y+{y}^{2})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{3}-2{y}^{2}+6y\,dy \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{8}{y}^{4}-\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3}+3{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =-2-\frac{16}{3}+12 \\  & =\frac{14}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
